candidates.title: Count open and urgent support tickets

demandEvidence.chore: Count open support tickets and identify how many are urgent.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Build a native n8n workflow to count how many are open, then how many of those open tickets are urgent.

ease.reason: A synthetic ticket list can test counts and flags, but the post gives no fields or urgency rule and no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional support team might value a queue summary; this challenge does not establish an AI-service buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can count supplied rows, but urgency criteria and live ticket access are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: Counting supplied records could repeat automatically; a person must define urgency, verify results and handle tickets.

evidence.reason: The post directly asks to count open and urgent tickets, but gives no recurrence, fields or operating rules.

candidates.reason: A synthetic-list experiment is concrete, but this repeats the support-ticket workflow and support-team customer of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6; mean 4.6 is also below threshold.

rejected.title: VM 9.0.0 mail reader for Emacs
rejected.reason: The Show HN excerpt only describes a mail reader and its community revival. It states no concrete chore, request for a tool or business idea, so there is no demand-backed experiment to assess.

rejected.title: Rouler Windows traffic steering
rejected.reason: The excerpt says the project was challenging and its maker is pleased with progress. It identifies no customer chore or request; inventing network administration duties from the product title would be unsupported.

rejected.title: Document processing extraction project
rejected.reason: The excerpt is a maker claim about the project’s document extraction performance, not a stated customer chore, request or business idea. It cannot support a demand-first candidate.

rejected.title: Count open and urgent support tickets
rejected.reason: The concrete count-and-urgency task was assessed with a bounded synthetic-list experiment, scoring 5/4/5/4/5 (mean 4.6). Reject as the same support-ticket workflow and professional support-team customer as recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6; the source also leaves fields and urgency rules unspecified.

rejected.title: Debug and finish an existing Make automation
rejected.reason: The post requests help completing one existing Make build, but provides no particular failure or repeatable diagnostic chore. A troubleshooting output would require invented details; no candidate is scored.

rejected.title: Shopify B2B checkout and local pickup issue
rejected.reason: The excerpt only asks “How does this make any sense?” about a checkout behavior. It supplies no concrete task or request for a service, so a workflow or buyer cannot be grounded.

steps.message: Assessed all six sealed discussion assignments. One states a concrete support-ticket count task, but it duplicates the recent support inbox workflow/customer and scores below threshold; the other five excerpts do not establish a concrete chore. No post proposed.
